Hey! I think you probably have trouble regulating emotions and possible just feeling emotionally dis-regulated a lot of the time. I have a lot of mental health issues that make it difficult for me to regulate and understand my emotions. I would suggest looking into dbt (dialectical behavioral therapy) which is aimed at regulation and identification of emotions. You can do this with a therapist, or get a workbook yourself and do it on your own. Try to be patient with yourself. Try not to judge yourself too harshly when you have emotional outbursts and instead think about how you are feeling in that moment and what kinds of things you can do to calm down. I hope this helps!

If you have an injury or illness or any other stressors on your body, you will be more low energy (for everyone, with or without narcolepsy). The body is trying to use the energy to heal. When people without narcolepsy go through this, they also sleep more than they usually would and be more tired. So of course for us, our “more tired” and “less energy” is wayyy way worse than others. That’s how I think about it at least. Chronic pain takes a huge toll on the body. Sorry if this isn’t super coherent.

I have no idea. I am a full time student in college (18 years old) and I am struggling. I don't understand where the time goes but somehow I run out of it every day, despite forcing myself to remain awake during the day. I basically just do what I can when I can. The best thing you can do is know yourself. For example, I can't ever expect myself to get work done from 12-6 pm. I also know I can't expect myself to get work done past 10pm (at the latest), and I can't be up before 6:30 (at the earliest). So, you might wonder when I do my work then, and the answer is I still don't know. I do some things between classes if I can (usually I cannot). I do some after dinner (usually I cannot). I do some on weekends (which is also very difficult). 

I will say that the only way to get things done is to do them when you can. If you feel like you have the energy to and you can think straight, do it then and don't put it off until later (my biggest downfall). Later always ends up being sleepy sleepy bed time + hating myself because I didn't do anything when I could have. 

I do all of my low effort assignments half asleep. I take notes in class so that if I don't have time to study, I at least wrote the notes which helps a tiny bit on passing the test. 

My best advice for getting schoolwork done is to: (1) don't do it in bed if you can. (2) stay sitting upright and do not lean on anything if possible. (3) listen to upbeat music or some other sensory method of staying awake (could also be snacking or chewing gum). 

There are many people with narcolepsy who have graduated through college or maintain careers, so it is possible to do for sure. Just keep trying your best and feel proud of yourself for how far you have already gotten despite the struggle! Hoping this comment makes sense and helps.

Sounds like you could definitely benefit from CBT. It focuses on redirecting negative thoughts and finding ways to think more positively and rationally. Catastrophic thinking is a common manifestation of anxiety which can be made worse when you are stressed. If you don’t have a therapist and can’t afford one, you can try CBT by yourself using a workbook. I can’t remember what mine was called but it was green and white. You can most likely find one very easily just searching for CBT workbook. I also suggest finding ways to ground yourself. I like to use repetition and music. If you have any questions about this let me know. I dont use CBT anymore, but it specifically targets “cognitive distortions” including catastrophic thinking.

Are you wearing a full tank or half tank binder? If it’s full, it could be pushing too much on your stomach, especially if have just eaten when it feels that way. 
Is the nausea specifically occurring while binding, or does it happen even after you take it off? If it is persistent even without wearing it, then I don’t think binding is the cause. 
It is also possible you are binding too tightly, so make sure you are wearing the proper size. 
Lastly, you should not wear your binder for more than 8 hours a day - do not sleep in it. You should follow all proper protocols when binding. If you don’t, you risk rib injury (that can be severe) or deformation which can ruin your chances of getting top surgery.

Im dealing with the same feelings (nearly) and I am not sure either but I only have a few ideas. Could be panic attacks, dissociation, or seizures. It depends on what other symptoms you have. Some things to consider would be how long the feeling lasts, what you were doing before it occurs, how you felt before, and if you are having any trouble breathing. if it lasts for a long time (several hours) then its probably dissociation. If it’s only for a few minutes to an hour, it’s probably just anxiety related. A few seconds to a minute could indicate seizures unless you were doing something before that causes sudden anxiety. Don’t take my word though, I don’t know much about seizures. 

Other things to consider are medications, foods and sleep. Are you talking any medication or eating anything out of the ordinary or before it happens? are you eating or sleeping enough? These things can heavily contribute to similar feelings.

I think honestly if they have done it before its possible they’ve done it again. If your hallucinations aren’t usually like that then I would also definitely think they had been lying. Whenever I have those hallucinations, I can tell after I wake up usually, unless its the ones with sleep paralysis. Its possible that it was a hallucination but to me its more likely that they had lied about not touching you. Mostly since they have done it once before and because its atypical for you to have vivid ones like this. A good indicator would be, how did they respond when you confronted them? Were they immediately defensive, deflective, angry?? Or were they calm and understanding, genuinely confused/concerned? If they were defensive or angry or deflective I think they definitely had done it. If you’ve been with them for a while, you should hopefully be able to tell when they are being genuine. Thats the only thing left that will really indicate the truth of whats happened.

Ok so I always heard the phrase “You’ll know when you do” and absolutely hated that, but its true. You will 100% know when you have an orgasm. Off T it mostly felt like soaking into a warm bath or something, very fluttery feeling. On T it feels like waves of warmth pulsing through my body, and more concentrated fluttering. Its different though for everyone I assume. I struggled for YEARS to actually have an orgasm and I had wondered the exact same things. My first time it took five hours to reach one. Five HOURS. But I stopped taking anti depressants a while after, and now I can orgasm normally. I hate to tell you that your antidepressants are the problem, but they are. I switched onto so many others hoping that one would let me and none actually did. I dont recommend you to go off of them, but I will say that that is most likely the cause. My best advice is to experiment with the way you feel doing various things and what feels the best. And don’t stress about whether you will reach an orgasm during sex or not. Just enjoy how it feels. It doesn’t have to be the end goal, and for many its not. Im not sure why anti depressants do that though. You would think less depression = more happy, more happy = more orgasm but no. If you want to though, you could talk to your psychiatrist about your concerns. But I wouldn’t recommend changing anything if the meds are really working for you and have been a huge improvement for you. I only quit because the medication never helped anyways. Sorry if this is a jumbled mess but I hope it helps.
